rounds.proof_sketch: With size=524288, idx=524287 is reachable (block 2047, thread 255). Original: 524287 < 524288 = TRUE (loads value). Mutated: 524287 < 524287 = FALSE (sets 0). Last element is always excluded from sum in mutant.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation tightens the boundary check from idx < size to idx < size - 1, causing the very last element (index 524287) to be excluded from the parallel reduction. With total_elements = 524288, the thread handling idx = 524287 will load 0.0f instead of the actual element loss. This causes systematic undercounting of the total loss by exactly one element's contribution. The mutant survived initial testing likely because random values spread across all elements make the single missing element's contribution negligible relative to tolerance.
rounds.kill_strategy: Set all elements to zero except the last element (index [127, 4095]) with a very large prediction-target difference. This concentrates all the loss in the single element that gets skipped by the mutant, maximizing the observable difference.
rounds.recommendations: Boundary mutations in reduction kernels are highly killable by concentrating meaningful values at boundary indices. Test coverage should always include cases where critical computation occurs at the first and last elements of reduction ranges.

def generate_inputs(device):
    predictions = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    targets = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    # Set last element to have large difference - this is the element skipped by mutant
    predictions[127, 4095] = 100000.0
    targets[127, 4095] = 0.0
    return [predictions, targets]
